A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VOCSIM benchmark. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original embedding evaluations across 19 subsets, ablation and robustness experiments, and HEAR, avian-perception, and mouse-classification results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds domain-level ranking analysis and a Whisper-Small evaluation.

M1.justification: Frozen feature extraction, pooling, per-subset label-free PCA, distance functions, and benchmark algorithms remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions of transductive evaluation and subset-specific AE/VAE training match procedures already documented in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 19 VOCSIM subsets and the same external-validation tasks. The four domain groupings in v2 reorganize existing coverage; Whisper-Small introduces no new dataset or task.

E2.justification: V2 adds Whisper-Small as an evaluated comparator to Large-v3 in Table 4. Existing foundation-model, AE/VAE, sequence-matching, and downstream comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: The new scale experiment runs the pipeline with Whisper-Small, reporting EWMTF with cosine distance. Large-v3 retains its PCA/Spearman configuration, so this is not a comparison holding every setting fixed. Existing experiments retain their preprocessing, splits, and evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds domain-disaggregated analysis and tests ranking consistency with and without the environmental subset. Section 5.4 adds the model-scale comparison. Existing pooling, DTW, label-noise, clustering, and layer analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the 300-resample bootstrap intervals, 1,000-label-permutation tests, and downstream fold standard deviations. The new analyses provide descriptive point summaries without adding repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: New results include domain summaries and mean GSR ranking agreement of Kendall's tau = 0.60, or 0.87 excluding environmental audio. Table 4 adds Whisper-Small P@1/GSR scores of 57.4/28.7 on public sets and 5.7/29.1 on blind sets. Previously reported main and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Metric definitions, separation-score derivations, and AE/VAE loss equations remain unchanged. Expanded Spearman and PCA discussion supplies explanatory rationale rather than a new formal analysis or proof.

C1.justification: V2 adds an abstract-level claim of stable GSR rankings across domains and explicitly confines the headline OOD conclusion to cross-lingual speech. The benchmark, GSR contribution, and downstream-validation claims otherwise remain.

C2.justification: V2 newly interprets domain-dependent P@1 rankings as pretraining alignment and comparatively stable GSR rankings as a more domain-invariant property. It adds a capacity-based interpretation of the scale experiment and explicitly treats ESC-50 as a robustness check rather than support for broad environmental conclusions.

D1.justification: Appendix B replaces anonymous code/data destinations with named VOCSIM resources and supplies a leaderboard described as maintained, replacing v1's promised post-review release. Much of the newly emphasized protocol detail already appeared in v1's appendices.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to existing audio benchmarks remain unchanged. The hubness reference emphasized in v2 Section 4.2 was already cited in v1's appendix; bibliography edits concern formatting and metadata.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract, protocol explanation, and conclusion, condenses external-validation prose, and adds a domain-analysis subsection and acknowledgements. The overall organization and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds domain-summary and model-scale Tables 3 and 4, relocates existing displays through text reflow, and improves pseudocode formatting. Existing figures are retained, and the extensive appendix result tables preserve their content and structure.

improvement.justification: Domain-disaggregated reporting makes model rankings easier to interpret, while explicit speech-only OOD framing better aligns conclusions with the evaluated coverage. Updated resource information also improves usability. The gains are limited: underlying benchmark results remain unchanged, and differing distance choices weaken the new experiment's attribution of performance differences specifically to model size.
